clue.text: The courage with which Virginia confronts a menacing look

parts.note: VA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
to lour (or lower) is to scowl or look threatening, and a lour is such a look

explanation.surface: A soldier from Virginia bravely faces down someone glaring at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronts' means stands in front of, so the state comes first; 'lour' is an old word for scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Valour is bravery, especially in battle, a synonym for courage.

clue.text: Agreed to be in excellent health

definitions.meaning: said as a reply meaning 'all right, I accept'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a word of consent ('all right then') and a literal statement that someone is thriving physically.

clue.text: The woman has nothing, but she's a sweetheart

parts.note: a lady is a woman
love means nil, a score of nothing in tennis

explanation.surface: A woman with no possessions is nonetheless a lovely, kind person.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring LOVE means zero, so 'nothing' gives LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladylove is an old-fashioned word for a man's beloved, a synonym for sweetheart.

clue.text: Trendy topper taken up in America

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, hence smart or fashionable

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word for topper is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a topper is a top hat, so a hat

explanation.surface: A fashionable top hat is picked up somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: U (as in 'U and non-U') is a crossword convention for upper-class or posh. The definition is loose: the answer is a state within America rather than America itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, a part of the country named.

clue.text: Want to inflict a blemish on a large town

parts.note: to scar is to mark with a blemish
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to disfigure an entire metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or shortage, which is what scarcity is.

clue.text: Heath finds a basis for discussion

definitions.meaning: open land shared by the public, such as a village green or moor
points both sides agree on, from which talks can begin

explanation.definitionFit: Unenclosed land everyone may use is a literal public expanse, while the figurative sense is shared views that make negotiation possible.

clue.text: Wind up the dance

definitions.meaning: to wind a line in on a spool, as an angler does
a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance

explanation.definitionFit: A fishing reel winds line in, and a reel is also a brisk folk dance.

clue.text: Just the flowers for Miss Murdoch on an English Sunday

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was the Anglo-Irish novelist

explanation.surface: A bouquet is the right gift for the novelist on a Sunday in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris Murdoch (1919-99) was an Anglo-Irish novelist and philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are garden plants with showy blue or purple blooms, so they are flowers.

clue.text: To utter a cry of pain is cowardly, ly

parts.note: to yell is to shout out
ow is the cry someone gives when hurt

explanation.surface: Crying out when hurt is supposedly a sign of weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow is informal for lacking courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for timid or lacking courage, as in 'yellow-bellied'.

clue.text: Scurrilous left-wing paper which arouses fury

definitions.meaning: a derisive name for a communist or socialist newspaper
from 'a ... to a bull', something guaranteed to provoke anger

explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a low-grade newspaper and red means communist, while the idiom about a bull names any provocation.

clue.text: The measure of empire

definitions.meaning: the British system of weights and measures, such as pints and miles
belonging to an empire or emperor

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both the traditional British system of units and anything relating to an empire.

clue.text: He has found employment at last

definitions.text: He has found employment at last

parts.words: He has found employment at last
parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block used by a cobbler, so someone working at a last mends footwear, not someone finally getting a job

explanation.surface: A long-unemployed man has finally landed a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' seems to mean 'finally', but a last is the wooden or metal form on which shoes are shaped and mended.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler fixing footwear works over a last, the shoe-shaped mould of the trade.

clue.text: Shakespeare's determination

definitions.meaning: William Shakespeare, familiarly known by the short form of his first name

explanation.definitionFit: The bard's first name shortened is the same as the word for resolve or willpower.

clue.text: Church has a very large following in total confusion

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, meaning very large

explanation.surface: A church in a state of utter disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... following' sets A and OS after CH. OS (outsize) is a garment-label abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete disorder, a synonym for total confusion.

clue.text: Emperor one Roman found loveless and inhuman

indicators.note: love is the tennis score zero, written as the letter O, so loveless means lose that letter
read as in-human-less: the word for a human being, a man, is taken out

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler is judged to be cold-hearted and cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes O from ONE, leaving NE; 'inhuman' takes MAN from ROMAN, leaving RO. 'loveless and inhuman' reads like a verdict on the emperor but is pure instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the Roman ruler of AD 54-68, notorious for cruelty.

clue.text: Everyone alas, is calm

parts.note: all means everyone
ay is an old exclamation of sorrow, like alas

explanation.surface: Despite regrets, everybody is serene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calm' looks like an adjective after 'is' but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay fears is to soothe or quieten them, so to calm.

clue.text: Where draught beer is readily available?

definitions.text: Where draught beer is readily available?

parts.words: Where draught beer is readily available?
parts.note: beer drawn from a barrel through a tap, and figuratively anything ready for immediate use

explanation.surface: Asking which pub serves beer from the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer flows from a tap, and the phrase also means ready whenever needed.

clue.text: Hanging out the clothes neatly side by side

definitions.text: Hanging out the clothes neatly side by side

parts.words: Hanging out the clothes neatly side by side
parts.note: pinning washing on a line with every clothes peg at the same height, also an idiom for being neck and neck

explanation.surface: Someone carefully arranges laundry on the washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means drawing equal in a contest; the clue pictures it literally, with clothes pegs in a level row.
explanation.definitionFit: Being equal in a race or contest is pictured as clothes pegs at matching height on a line.

clue.text: The strict boss may take it to manufacture company product

definitions.text: The strict boss may take it

parts.note: a firm is a business or company
a line is a range of goods a maker sells

explanation.surface: A demanding manager decides to make the company's goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manufacture' is surface padding linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict boss adopts an unyielding stance, which is taking a hard policy position.

clue.text: Intervening period is an era of austerity

definitions.meaning: read literally as a stingy, penny-pinching time

explanation.definitionFit: The interval between events is the standard sense, while taken as two words it describes a miserly, frugal era.

clue.text: What the cheating cabbie may do to his passengers

definitions.text: What the cheating cabbie may do to his passengers

parts.words: What the cheating cabbie may do to his passengers
parts.note: a taxi trip in the literal sense, and in the idiomatic sense swindling or deceiving someone

explanation.surface: A dishonest taxi driver fleeces his fares.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cheat or con, and a cab driver literally drives people around.

clue.text: Glass is a topic needing analysis

indicators.note: analysing breaks something down into parts, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel is a subject worth studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing analysis' rearranges A TOPIC into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copita is a tulip-shaped glass traditionally used for sherry.

clue.text: Plead with an individual, but get only a harsh dismissal

parts.note: to beg is to plead
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone appeals to a person but is curtly sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command to leave at once, a brusque way of sending someone off.

clue.text: Frank makes an appeal to a writer

parts.note: O is an exclamation used in pleading, as in 'O, help me'
a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank sends a letter of request to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but means candid. 'a writer' is the instrument, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means candid and honest, a synonym for frank.

clue.text: Haggard father of the House of Lancaster

definitions.text: father of the House of Lancaster
definitions.meaning: John of ..., Duke of Lancaster, ancestor of the Lancastrian kings

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lean and drawn, and John of Gaunt founded the English royal line of Lancaster.

clue.text: A lot of males have the last word

parts.note: men is a group of males

explanation.surface: A crowd of men always insist on winning the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' is literal: the word said at the end of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of prayers and hymns, so it is literally the final word.

clue.text: Tease in a most witless way

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the clue's words most witless, spanning the join between them

explanation.surface: Someone mocks another in a thoroughly foolish manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tease' is the verb sense: to twit someone is to taunt them.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is to taunt or tease them good-humouredly.

clue.text: Come down to earth

definitions.meaning: to touch down, as an aircraft does
ground or terrain as opposed to sea

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft touching down arrives, and the noun means dry ground or soil.

clue.text: A pressing task, it is, to make wrought metal

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
work means a job or task

explanation.surface: Ironing clothes is described as one way of shaping metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' suggests urgent but means smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironwork is decorative work in wrought iron, such as gates and railings.

clue.text: Thanks to record success I acquire a Pacific island

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
a hit is a successful record in the charts

explanation.surface: A chart-topping single lets the singer buy a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ta' is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Giving beer to a right-winger is dicey

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: Buying a drink for a Conservative politician is a risky move.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on chance, from the Latin for dice, so risky or uncertain.

clue.text: Stick the advertisement in this spot

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement
here means this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up the poster in this location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like an order to put the ad up but is the definition, the verb meaning cling.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay fixed, a synonym for stick.
